text:
support-jordan: Hey team — customer @acme-prod reporting sudden spike in latency (200-800ms) and intermittent 401s starting ~08:55 UTC. Affected region: Frankfurt customers hitting our EU endpoint are seeing traffic land in us-east per their traceroutes. Billing also spiked. Can someone triage? :warning:
ingrid-eng: Thanks, checking. Do we have a recent DNS/geoip push or any shard key rotations?

support-jordan: No push on their account. They attached a curl trace showing region header set to us-east from eu clients.

support-jordan: curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
* Connected to api.redwood.example (54.239.XX.XX) port 443
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer <token>
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-redwood-region: us-east-1
< x-request-id: r-abc123

alex-sre: Interesting — `x-redwood-region` header comes from our edge that served the request. If eu clients see us-east header it implies resolver answered with an A that points to us-east edge. Any hints in dig?

support-jordan: They ran dig with one of their ISP resolvers: 

```
$ dig @203.0.113.12 api.redwood.example +short
54.239.XX.XX
```

support-jordan: That resolver is an ISP NAT resolver in Frankfurt, expected to return eu IPs.

ingrid-eng: I'm pulling up our DNS prefill maps and geoip mappings. We rotated a shard key for resolver affinity yesterday during a runtime rollout — it rebalanced which resolver cohorts map to which edge pool. Could be a mis-applied mapping in the new shard config.

dan-ops: Also saw a failed S3 sync for the geodb publish at 08:49 UTC with retries — might mean some edge boxes had stale geoip db momentarily. Logging: `geodb-sync: WARN missing s3://geo-updates/2026-03-17/fragment-12`

alex-sre: That explains inconsistent behavior. Two concurrent problems: (1) shard rotation changed resolver->edge mapping, (2) some edges still had an old geoip DB so they applied the wrong locality fallback. Combined, certain resolver caches got handed a us-east answer.

product-maria: Customer is seeing 401s — why auth?

ingrid-eng: Our tokens are region-scoped for some Dedicated customers. If a token was minted for eu-central and a request lands in us-east edge that doesn't accept eu tokens, it returns 401. For hosted customers it's usually fine, but acme-prod uses a regional token policy.

support-jordan: Customer provided tcpdump showing SYN->our us-east IP, then TLS handshake then 401. They said this started right after we did 'resolver-shard-roll' yesterday morning.

alex-sre: Quick repro steps for infra to confirm: 1) pick a Frankfurt ISP resolver IP and query A for api.redwood.example; 2) run geoip lookup against the returned IP; 3) check edge `edge-status` for that IP and the geodb version.

ingrid-eng: I ran that against one resolver seen in their tcpdump: 
```
$ dig @203.0.113.12 api.redwood.example +short
54.239.XX.XX
$ geoiplookup 54.239.XX.XX
GeoIP Country: US
```
Edge status for that IP shows `geodb:v2026-03-16` on host `edge-752` while current is `v2026-03-17`.

dan-ops: So some edges didn't get the latest geodb fragment due to the S3 sync error and then the shard rotation assigned resolver cohorts to those stale edges. Result: eu resolvers cached us-east answers. TTLs are 300s, so the effect can linger.

support-jordan: Customer wants immediate mitigation — low tolerance. Suggestions?

alex-sre: Short-term mitigations: 
- Force-override routing policy for acme-prod to prefer `eu-central` model set (will route via control-plane rule, bypassing resolver mapping) — low-risk and reversible.
- Purge/flush DNS prefill cache for affected resolver cohorts if we can identify them (we have a purge API, but may not reach ISP caches).
- Roll forward geodb fragments to all edges (re-run S3 sync/publish and confirm checksums).

ingrid-eng: I'm pushing the geodb fragment re-sync now and watching. Also rolling back the shard rotation is an option but is higher risk for new traffic patterns.

deploy-bot: geodb-publish v2026-03-17 started at 09:28 UTC, 12/12 edges updated, checksums verified.

dan-ops: After the sync, I triggered prefill cache invalidation for cohort keys: `cohort-42, cohort-47, cohort-58`. TTLs on ISP side still mean some stale answers may persist for a few minutes.

support-jordan: I applied routing-policy override for acme-prod and asked them to confirm. They report latency dropped to normal and 401s stopped after ~2 min. :white_check_mark:

product-maria: Can we add a safety: if geodb publish fails, block shard rotations that depend on new mappings? Looks like a race.

ingrid-eng: Agreed. Filing an action: add precondition to shard-rotation workflow to verify geodb publish status and edge checksums. Also adding better monitoring on resolver affinity reassignments.

support-jordan: Notes for ticket to customer: explanation + mitigation steps + ETA for permanent fix. Will ask them to monitor for 1hr.

alex-sre: Follow-ups: (1) add pre-rotation S3 publish verification, (2) consider reducing TTL temporarily during rollout windows, (3) improve dashboard to show per-edge geodb version.

support-jordan: Closing loop — customer confirms stable at 09:34 UTC. I'll keep ticket open until 10:30 for post-checks. Thanks all. :pray:
